Chapter 119: 0116 President Lu Is Not Only Resourceful, But Also Extremely Well-Connected

The headquarters of Microsoft Research Asia was located in Zhongguancun, so Dong Qianqiu was back at the company after a short walk.

Chen Guiliang shook his hand to welcome him back, then asked curiously, "No matter how few rights interns have, they wouldn't just be thrown to do menial chores, would they?"

Dong Qianqiu explained, "After an intern starts, they're assigned to a group with a mentor. Right now, there are seven groups working on sixteen core projects simultaneously. They hire over two hundred interns every year, so the competition among interns is especially fierce. I joined my group relatively late and got screwed over by another intern."

Chen Guiliang said with a laugh, "Interns play office politics too?"

Dong Qianqiu sighed and said, "I didn't expect it either. The whole group was incredibly busy, with the old project already at a critical stage. The other interns in the group were basically all working on that old project."

"Only me and one other intern were in charge of doing the preliminary literature review for a new project. That means systematically collecting, categorizing, analyzing, and summarizing academic papers, technical reports, industry news, and other materials."

"That intern tricked me. He said since I was new, I should get on good terms with everyone. He told me to serve tea and water to the group members to get my face known, so we'd get along better later. I actually believed his bullshit and rushed to help everyone with unnecessary chores, acting like a sycophantic bootlicker!"

"And what was the result? He went to our mentor and reported on me, saying I was a procrastinator who only thought about slacking off, and that I was going around serving tea and water to suck up to people. He also secretly shredded some of the literature I had organized. I even suspect he overwrote it multiple times to prevent recovery!"

Chen Guiliang asked, "Your mentor didn't do anything about it?"

"He and the mentor are alumni," Dong Qianqiu said dejectedly. "Besides, the mentor is very busy and has no time to investigate the truth. Since he reported on me first, the mentor naturally believed him. The mentor even criticized me and told me to fix my attitude. I got so angry I argued back at the mentor. Then, the mentor told me to go do menial chores to reflect, and stopped assigning me any work at all."

Chen Guiliang lamented inwardly: This brother is still too young.

Completely unguarded against others.

Why would that intern screw over Dong Qianqiu?

It was simply to kick Dong Qianqiu out and complete the project's literature review all by himself. Even if another intern was brought in to help later, he would have already done the main work. First, it would allow him to showcase his abilities, and second, if a paper was written afterward, he could guarantee his position as the first author.

Guo Feng, who had been sitting nearby and listening, scratched his head and said, "Big companies are so complicated. If I went there, I'd definitely get screwed over too."

Dong Qianqiu said, "I just never even considered that possibility. This is Microsoft Research Asia! Everyone should be working together with one heart and striving for a common goal!"

Chen Guiliang said with a laugh, "People that despicable are rare. Your luck is just too bad."

Dong Qianqiu said, "Actually, even if this hadn't happened, I was already thinking of coming back. There are too many interns there, and they're all top talents. It's incredibly difficult to stand out. If you can't make a name for yourself, you're stuck doing more marginal work. By the end of the one-year internship, you'd definitely have learned something, but not as much as I'd imagined. Most interns just get a paper published and then leave."

Chen Guiliang comforted him, "When our company gets bigger, we'll start a research institute too, and you can be the director then."

"I'm taking you seriously," Dong Qianqiu said.

"Absolutely. Let's go, time for a feast!"

This was the first team dinner since moving into the new office, and the friends who came to help were invited as well.

It was the middle of winter, perfect for Beijing hot pot.

Walking against the cold wind, Wu Meng asked, "It's already December, why hasn't it snowed in Beijing yet?"

Deng Chen chimed in, "I know, right? I'm still waiting to see the snow."

Ao Yanchen said, "It had already snowed by this time last year."

The freshmen from the south had been long anticipating the first snow in Beijing.

But Heaven just wouldn't let it snow!

"Who wants to go see 'A World Without Thieves'?"

"Is there a movie theater near the university?"

"School's been in session for so long, and you still haven't seen a movie?"

"Nope."

"I'm waiting for 'Kung Fu Hustle.' Stephen Chow hasn't made a new movie in a long time."

Chatting about everything from snow to movies, the group arrived laughing at the hot pot restaurant.

Copper pot hot pot.

They had the shop warm up the beer as well. Chen Guiliang raised his glass and said, "Today, the company finally has a decent office. Thanks to all the students who came to help, and thanks to my brothers and sisters for all their hard work these days. A toast to everyone!"

"To Boss Chen's overflowing wealth."

"To our company's booming business."

"Cheers!"

After a few glasses of beer, Ao Yanchen took out her camera, "Let me take a few pictures of everyone."

Bian Guanyue leaned toward Chen Guiliang and made a peace sign.

Guo Feng made a gun shape with his right thumb and index finger, placing it by his chin in a classic 007 pose.

Dong Qianqiu grinned foolishly at the camera.

Everyone struck different poses and expressions, all frozen in that moment.

By the time the hot pot meal was over, most of the friends were drunk, and they supported each other back to the dorms.

Chen Guiliang, however, took Bian Guanyue to a hotel.

Bian Guanyue had also had quite a bit to drink tonight. The effects of the alcohol hadn't faded even after a shower, and she hugged Chen Guiliang with a flushed face.

They had agreed to do... romantic things on Christmas, and they certainly couldn't go back on their word, but they could try other things.

After some cuddling, Bian Guanyue lay in Chen Guiliang's arms and said, "Our university also started a campus belle competition."

"What's your rank?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Bian Guanyue giggled, "Hehe, first for now. But very few people have voted. Xiaonei isn't that popular at our school yet."

Chen Guiliang said, "That's already quite a few. I specifically checked the data. Your school has over a thousand users. And they all grew organically from the initial seven people who sent out invitation codes. The campus belle competition will speed up registration. It'll probably grow to three or four thousand by Christmas."

"Our university only has a little over ten thousand students. I think only three or four thousand have computers in total," Bian Guanyue said.

Chen Guiliang said, "You can register without a computer."

"That's true," Bian Guanyue said, then asked, "Are you going back to your hometown for the New Year?"

Chen Guiliang said, "I can't get away from the company. There's still a lot to do."

Bian Guanyue said, "Then I'll stay and keep you company."

"Next New Year, I'll go with you to see your grandparents," Chen Guiliang said.

"Mhm," Bian Guanyue smiled happily.

"Go to sleep."

"I want to sleep while hugging you."

A new week began, and Chen Guiliang skipped class again, and again, and again.

He was a hundred percent going to fail English. He hadn't memorized a single word since starting university, and he skipped English class every other day.

He just really didn't want to learn it.

As for his other courses, whether he'd fail depended on fate.

Under Li Xunhuan's constant pressure for more content, Chen Guiliang's writing speed increased considerably.

Because Li Xunhuan had already started the promotion.

The guy truly had an incredible network. A whole bunch of famous authors like Han Han, Guo Xiaosi, Ning Caishen, Xing Yusen, Annie Baobei, Jin Hezai, Cai Jun... all promoted *Those Happenings in the Ming Dynasty* on their blogs at the same time.

It instantly attracted the attention of countless netizens and the media.

Li Xunhuan took the opportunity to leak information to several newspapers, saying that he had already signed the book and had given an unprecedented royalty share. He also mentioned that Chen Guiliang's Xiaonei had been valued at 5 million USD by venture capitalists, but he had refused the investment.

One stone sent a thousand ripples, and the media reported on it from all angles.

Several publishing houses protested, actively contacting newspapers to say that Li Xunhuan was ruining the publishing industry. A tiered share starting with a guaranteed 15% left no room for profit. Moreover, *Those Happenings in the Ming Dynasty* was simply not worth that price!

The debate raged on, both online and offline.

You can imagine the influence of blogs back then as being similar to Weibo more than ten years later.

Han Han was busy with car racing. After the publication of *Chang'an in Chaos*, he hadn't really been active online.

He updated his blog without any warning, but the content was just a single sentence: I recently discovered a good book called *Those Happenings in the Ming Dynasty*. It's being serialized on forums like Tianya and Rongshu Xia.

So perfunctory.

It was obviously a forced promotion.

The comment section was filled with all sorts of replies.

"Wow, Han Shao finally made an appearance."
